title: Replace deprecated @pplancq/postcss-config with minimal local config in @shelter-ui/css
body:
## Context

The `@shelter-ui/css` package depends on `@pplancq/postcss-config` (^3.0.6), which is now **deprecated** on npm:

> Deprecated: modern builders handle CSS transformation natively; these PostCSS plugins are redundant for recent browsers.

See: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pplancq/postcss-config

The deprecated package provided 3 plugins that are all redundant here:

| Plugin | Why it's redundant |
|---|---|
| `postcss-flexbugs-fixes` | IE10/11 flexbox workarounds — obsolete for modern browser targets |
| `postcss-preset-env` (stage 4) | Covered natively by **Lightning CSS**, used by Rsbuild/rslib for vendor prefixing and syntax downgrade (based on browserslist) |
| `postcss-normalize` | No-op in this project — no `@import "normalize"` statement exists in the stylesheets |

⚠️ **Unlike other projects, a pure removal is NOT possible here.** The current `packages/css/postcss.config.js` also adds `postcss-discard-duplicates`, which is still needed: rslib builds with `bundle: false`, so each `.scss` file is compiled separately and can emit duplicate CSS rules. Lightning CSS does not deduplicate across separate outputs.

## Task

Replace the shared config with a minimal local one:

1. Rewrite `packages/css/postcss.config.js` to keep **only** `postcss-discard-duplicates`:

   ```js
   import postcssDiscardDuplicates from "postcss-discard-duplicates";

   // eslint-disable-next-line import/no-default-export
   export default {
     plugins: [postcssDiscardDuplicates],
   };
   ```

2. Remove `"@pplancq/postcss-config": "^3.0.6"` from `devDependencies` in `packages/css/package.json` (keep `postcss-discard-duplicates`, already a direct dependency)
3. Regenerate `package-lock.json`
4. Run `npm run build` in `packages/css` and compare the generated CSS against the previous output (rules must be identical apart from the removal of preset-env/normalize no-ops)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `postcss.config.js` no longer imports `@pplancq/postcss-config`
- [ ] `@pplancq/postcss-config` removed from `packages/css/package.json`
- [ ] `postcss-discard-duplicates` is still applied (no duplicate rules in the built CSS)
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds and generated CSS is functionally unchanged

## References

- Deprecated package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pplancq/postcss-config
- rslib build config: `packages/css/rslib.config.mjs`

title: The kit installs as one plugin — a team that only wants the issue → PR lifecycle loads 17 components, a `Read` hook and two `dnx` servers where 12 components and no .NET would do
body:
## Problem The kit ships as **one** plugin, and half of its consumers only want half of it. A team on a Node or Python repo that installs it for the issue → pull request lifecycle (`create-issue`, `implement-issue`, `merge-pr`, `auto-dev`, …) also gets, in every session: - the `migrate-legacy` and `review-followups` skills and the five `/migrate*` commands — 561 + 586 + 518 bytes of description loaded on every turn for a pipeline they will never run (measured on `skills/*/SKILL.md` and `commands/migrate-*.md` frontmatter; `claude plugin details` counts 17 components where 12 are theirs); - `hooks/roseline-gate.sh`, a `PreToolUse` hook that fires on every `Read`, probes for `dnx`, and only then fails open (ADR 0002); - the `roseline` and `adr` MCP servers in `.mcp.json`, which Claude Code tries to start with `dnx … --yes` — on a machine without the .NET 10 SDK that is two red "failed to connect" lines at every session start; - `scripts/preflight.sh` reporting `MISSING ✗ dotnet SDK >= 8` and `MISSING ✗ RoselineMCP connected` and exiting 1, because `requirements.json` marks both `required` without saying **which skill** requires them. `plugin.json`'s own description already reads "… plus generic GitHub issue/PR lifecycle skills" — the two halves are named there, but nothing lets a consumer install one of them. The owner's stated constraint is that token spend decides whether the kit survives (`skills/auto-dev/references/token-economics.md`): shipping a pipeline a session cannot use is the cost the kit exists to avoid. ## Proposed solution A second plugin, **`ai-lifecycle-kit`**, served from this repository at `plugins/lifecycle/` — a manifest plus **symlinks** into the existing tree, so no file moves and both plugins ride the one version release-please bumps (ADR 0003): - `plugins/lifecycle/skills/` → `../../../skills/` for the ten lifecycle skills and `_shared`; `plugins/lifecycle/{hooks,scripts,decisions,templates}` and `{AGENTS.md,requirements.json,CONTEXT.md}` → the root ones, so `` (`/../..`) resolves to a complete kit root inside the installed copy. `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-*.md` are **copies**, not links — a symlinked command file is not discovered (measured below). - `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — name, version, description, `"hooks": "./hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json"`; **no `.mcp.json`** — the lifecycle plugin launches no server, so it needs no `dnx` and no .NET at all (the three skills that consult AdrMcp already fall back to grepping `docs/adr/` and say so; a consumer who wants it registers `dnx AdrMcp --yes` in their own MCP settings). `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` (`claude-hooks.json` minus the `Read` block) and the two command copies are **derived files** `scripts/host-adapters.py build` writes and `check` refuses when edited by hand, the same way it treats `gemini-extension.json` and `commands/*.toml`. - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` gains the entry `{"name": "ai-lifecycle-kit", "source": "./plugins/lifecycle"}`; `ai-migration-kit` stays exactly as it is. - `requirements.json`: the `dotnet SDK >= 8` and `RoselineMCP connected` entries get `requiredBy: ["migrate-legacy"]` (with the `token` the frontmatter gate demands), so preflight prints `[hard-required by: migrate-legacy]` on those lines. - `scripts/host-adapters.py check` grows the invariants that keep the lifecycle tree complete: every `skills/*/` directory outside the migration set is linked, nothing shipped matches `migrate|roseline`, no `.mcp.json` exists there, and every runtime `/` a lifecycle skill or script names resolves under `plugins/lifecycle/`. **Measured, not assumed** — four spikes on a scratch copy of this tree with `claude plugin marketplace add ` / `claude plugin install` / `claude plugin details`: | Shape | `details` inventory | |---|---| | a second marketplace entry with `source: "./"` and explicit `skills`/`commands`/`hooks`/`mcpServers` lists | the root `plugin.json` wins: 17 skills and commands, `roseline` + `adr` — the lists are ignored | | `plugins/lifecycle/` with a whole-directory `skills` symlink and an explicit 10-item `skills` list in its `plugin.json` | 12 skills: the `skills/` directory is always discovered, the list only *adds* | | `plugins/lifecycle/` with **per-skill directory symlinks**, symlinked command *files*, an `.mcp.json` with `adr` only, `hooks: ./hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` | 10 skills, `adr` only, `PreToolUse` = `Bash` only; the cache holds real directories (0 symlinks left, 2.0 MB) — but **no command registered**: a symlinked `.md` is not discovered even though the cache holds the file | | same, with the two command files **copied** and no `.mcp.json` | **12 components: the ten skills + `auto-dev-worker` + `auto-dev-merge`, 0 MCP servers, `PreToolUse` = `Bash` only** | Split, by side: | Side | Ships | |---|---| | **migration only** | `skills/migrate-legacy`, `skills/review-followups`, `commands/migrate-*.md`, `hooks/roseline-gate.sh`, the `roseline` server, scripts `audit-inventory.sh` · `dependency-health.sh` · `report-dashboard.py` · `contrast-check.py` · `followups.py` | | **lifecycle** (both plugins) | the other ten skills, `commands/auto-dev-*.md`, hooks `git-write-gate.sh` · `routing-context.sh` · `autodev-stop-gate.sh`, `skills/_shared/`, `scripts/tracker.sh` · `decide.sh` · the guards — and, in the full kit only, the `adr` server | ## Area area: ci ## Alternatives considered - **A second marketplace entry over the root with component lists** — the first thing tried; Claude Code ignores the entry's lists when the source carries a `plugin.json`, and a `skills/` directory at the plugin root is always discovered. Measured above. - **Two repositories** — forks `skills/_shared/`, `tests/_lib.sh`, release-please, `host-adapters.py` and the docs site, against the one-home doctrine (#324); rejected. - **`host-adapters.py build` copying the lifecycle files into `plugins/lifecycle/` instead of symlinking** — Windows-safe, but commits ~1.2 MB of duplicated skill text and a drift check over every byte of it. Kept as the upgrade path if a Windows consumer needs the lifecycle plugin. - **Do nothing, tell lifecycle users to set `ROSELINE_GATE=off`** — silences the hook, not the server start, the preflight verdict or the frontmatter cost. **Related:** #526 (the manifests and marketplaces `host-adapters.py` already checks), #556 (the JSON-validity step over those manifests), #323 (skill descriptions on a token budget), ADR-2, ADR-3, ADR-14
🧠 Brainstorm **Problem / context.** The coupling map is clean: no lifecycle skill executes a migration script. The only cross-side mention is a string list of script names in `skills/review-sessions/scripts/harvest.py` (error signatures it greps transcripts for), not a dependency. `implement-issue` step 06 mandates RoselineMCP for C# *target* repos — that rule stays on the lifecycle side on purpose: it applies to any consumer whose target repo has C#, and the gate fails open without `dnx` (ADR 0002), so a lifecycle install keeps the rule without bundling the server. The Claude Code plugin reference: paths in a manifest must stay under the plugin root (`../` is rejected); installed plugins are copied to a cache; "if you need to share files across plugins, use symlinks". The spikes above add what the reference does not say: a `skills/` directory at the plugin root is always discovered in full, so the only way to ship ten of twelve is a root whose `skills/` holds exactly ten; and discovery follows a symlinked *directory* but skips a symlinked *file*, so the two commands travel as copies. ADRs consulted through AdrMcp (semantic, accepted): consistent with ADR-3 (one version — the new manifest is one more release-please `extra-files` entry, bumped in the same release; the marketplace file carries no version, per #556) and ADR-14 (thin manifests over one tree — this is one more manifest and a set of links, not a second tree). ADR-2 is what makes leaving the roseline rule on the lifecycle side safe. ADR-6 is superseded by 14 and does not apply. **Approaches.** 1. **`plugins/lifecycle/` = manifest + per-skill symlinks** — no file moves, one version, the derived hooks map and command copies generated by the mechanism `host-adapters.py` already runs. Cost: symlinks in git (a first for this repo; a Windows checkout without `core.symlinks` gets text files, and the lifecycle plugin is broken there while the full kit is not); the routing table `routing-context.sh` injects still carries the `/migrate` row; AdrMcp is not bundled. 2. **`plugins/lifecycle/` = manifest + files copied by `host-adapters.py build`** — Windows-safe, ~1.2 MB duplicated and checked for drift on every PR; the upgrade path from 1 if a Windows consumer asks. 3. **Move the migration half out** (`plugins/migration/`) and make the root the lifecycle plugin — breaks every install line, every `/skills/migrate-legacy` path and ADR 12's naming stability; a major, for the same result as 1. **Recommendation.** Approach 1, because it is the smallest diff that the spike proved works, at the cost of the Windows ceiling named above — which approach 2 lifts without changing the plugin's shape, so nothing filed today is thrown away. **Assumptions.** The plugin is named `ai-lifecycle-kit` (install: `claude plugin install ai-lifecycle-kit@ai-migration-kit-marketplace`); the full bundle keeps its name and content; `review-followups` goes migration-side (it consolidates `migration/report.json`); the Codex marketplace (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`) and the other hosts' manifests are untouched here.
📋 Spec **Goal.** A Claude Code user can install the issue → PR lifecycle alone, with no .NET prerequisite, no roseline hook and no bundled MCP server, from this repository and at the same version as the full kit. **Scope.** `plugins/lifecycle/` (new; its two commands derived), `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` (derived), `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `release-please-config.json`, `requirements.json`, `scripts/host-adapters.py`, `README.md`, `docs/_data/hosts.yml`, `docs/adr/`, and the golden suites that already own those files. **Non-goals:** moving any file; a second version or changelog; the Codex / Copilot / Gemini / pi manifests; filtering the routing table per plugin. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph tree["one tree, one version (ADR 3)"] S[skills/ ×12 + _shared] C[commands/ ×7] H[hooks/ + lifecycle-hooks.json] M[.mcp.json] R[scripts/ decisions/ templates/ AGENTS.md requirements.json] end A["ai-migration-kit\n(root, unchanged)"] --> S & C & H & M & R L["ai-lifecycle-kit\nplugins/lifecycle/\n(no .mcp.json)"] -. "10 + _shared dir symlinks" .-> S L -- "2 copies (derived)" --> C L -. "dir symlink" .-> H L -. "dir / file symlinks" .-> R ``` **Public surface.** - `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (hand-written, versioned): ```json { "name": "ai-lifecycle-kit", "displayName": "AI Lifecycle Kit", "version": "2.7.0", "description": "The GitHub issue → pull request lifecycle of ai-migration-kit (create-issue, implement-issue, merge-pr, auto-dev, triage-backlog, …) without the .NET migration pipeline: no bundled MCP server, no roseline hook, no .NET prerequisite.", "author": { "name": "Philippe Matray" }, "license": "MIT", "hooks": "./hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json", "keywords": ["github", "issues", "pull-requests", "agent-skills"] } ``` No `skills`, `commands` or `mcpServers` field — the directories are discovered, and the spike showed a list cannot narrow discovery anyway. No `.mcp.json` next to it. - Symlinks (git mode `120000`, relative targets): `plugins/lifecycle/skills/{_shared,auto-dev,create-issue,debug-issue,deliver-issue,implement-issue,merge-pr,profile-repo,review-sessions,setup-repo,triage-backlog}` → `../../../skills/`; `plugins/lifecycle/{hooks,scripts,decisions,templates}` → `../../`; `plugins/lifecycle/{AGENTS.md,requirements.json,CONTEXT.md}` → `../../` (file links are fine here: nothing *discovers* them, the scripts read them from the dereferenced cache). - Derived by `host-adapters.py build` (added to `generated(repo)`, so `check` refuses a hand edit): `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` = `hooks/claude-hooks.json` with the `PreToolUse` block whose `matcher` is `Read` removed; `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-worker.md` and `auto-dev-merge.md` = byte copies of `commands/` (a symlinked command file is not discovered — spike 3). - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` → `plugins[1]` = `{"name": "ai-lifecycle-kit", "source": "./plugins/lifecycle", "description": }`. `plugins[0]` stays `ai-migration-kit` (`tests/host-adapters/test.sh` case T reads index 0). - `release-please-config.json` → one more `extra-files` entry: `{"type": "json", "path": "plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json", "jsonpath": "$.version"}`; `scripts/host-adapters.py` `VERSIONED` gains the same path (cases K/L and the CI JSON step then cover it for free). - `requirements.json` — on `dotnet SDK >= 8`: `"requiredBy": ["migrate-legacy"], "token": ".NET SDK"`; on `RoselineMCP connected`: `"requiredBy": ["migrate-legacy"], "token": "RoselineMCP"`. Both tokens already appear in `skills/migrate-legacy/SKILL.md`'s `compatibility`, which `tests/skills/check-frontmatter.py` walks for `tools` and `mcps` alike. `level` stays `required`: preflight is the pipeline's phase-0 gate and still exits 1; the line now names its owner. - `scripts/host-adapters.py` `invariants()` — constants `LIFECYCLE = "plugins/lifecycle"`, `MIGRATION_SKILLS = {"migrate-legacy", "review-followups"}`, `MIGRATION_COMMANDS = re.compile(r"^migrate")`; refusals, one line each: - `REFUSE: plugins/lifecycle/skills/ is missing — every skill outside MIGRATION_SKILLS is linked` (for each `skills/*/` directory, `_shared` included) - `REFUSE: plugins/lifecycle/ links to '', which is not ` (a symlink whose resolved target is not the root file/directory of the same name, or a real file where a link is expected) - `REFUSE: plugins/lifecycle ships '', which matches migrate|roseline` (over every entry under `skills/`, `commands/`, and the hooks map's `command` values) - `REFUSE: plugins/lifecycle ships an .mcp.json — the lifecycle plugin launches no server (ADR 16)` - `REFUSE: plugins/lifecycle lacks '', which names` — for every `/` spelled in the linked skills' `.md` and `scripts/*`, in `skills/_shared/`, `scripts/*.sh|py`, `hooks/*.sh` and `AGENTS.md` (regex `/([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)`), the path must exist under `plugins/lifecycle/` after link resolution — **except** a path under `docs/`, `tests/` or `.claude/`, which is a documentation pointer, not a runtime dependency (today: `/docs/methodology.md`, `/docs/backlog.md`, `/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, one `/tests/…`). - `README.md` → *Install › Claude Code*: a second fenced block, `claude plugin install ai-lifecycle-kit@ai-migration-kit-marketplace`, introduced by one sentence ("Only the issue → pull request lifecycle, no .NET, no bundled MCP server: …"), one sentence saying the two are either/or, and one saying AdrMcp is registered by hand if wanted (`dnx AdrMcp --yes`, .NET 10 SDK) and the skills grep `docs/adr/` without it. `docs/_data/hosts.yml` → `claude-code.then` gains the same sentence; the `install` list is unchanged (case R checks those lines verbatim in README, and a third line there would render as a third command to run). - `docs/adr/0016-a-lifecycle-only-plugin-is-a-manifest-and-symlinks-over-the-one-tree.md` — MADR 4.0, `status: accepted`, tags `distribution`, `release`; `code_refs` `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `scripts/host-adapters.py`; a row in `docs/adr/README.md`. **Validation rules.** Every symlink target is relative and resolves inside the repository. `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is valid JSON at the release-please version. `hooks/hooks.json` never exists (case I). `plugins/lifecycle/.mcp.json` never exists. **Edge cases.** - *Windows checkout without symlink support* (`core.symlinks=false`, the git-for-Windows default outside Developer Mode): the links check out as one-line text files and the lifecycle plugin's cache holds no skills. The full kit is unaffected. Named in the ADR's consequences and in README's sentence; the remedy, if asked for, is the copy-by-`build` alternative — same plugin shape, no consumer-visible change. - *Commands must be real files.* Spike 3 (symlinked `.md`) registered none; spike 4 (copied) registered both. Hence the `build`-generated copies, drift-checked like every other derived file. - *AdrMcp.* Not bundled: `create-issue`, `implement-issue` and `merge-pr` already say "ADRs read from files; AdrMcp not connected" and grep `docs/adr/*.md` — the documented degradation in `requirements.json`. A consumer who wants the server registers it in their own MCP settings. - *Both plugins installed at once*: skills register twice under two plugin prefixes; README says either/or. No guard — Claude Code owns that namespace. - *A new skill lands in `skills/`*: the first invariant refuses until it is linked or added to `MIGRATION_SKILLS` — the decision is forced at the PR, never discovered by a consumer. - *A lifecycle skill starts reading a new `/`*: the fourth invariant refuses until the path is linked. - *`git ls-files`-driven gates* (`tracked-exec-globs.txt`, `parse-sweep.sh`, `decision-check.py`): a symlink is one index entry of mode `120000`, never a file under it, and no pathspec there starts with `plugins/` — nothing double-counts. `tests/skills/check-frontmatter.py` globs `skills/*/SKILL.md` and `commands/*.md` from the root only; the two command copies under `plugins/lifecycle/commands/` are outside both globs. **Assumptions.** Plugin name `ai-lifecycle-kit`; commit type `feat(plugin)` (dry-run: `scripts/release-title-gate.sh "feat(plugin): …" plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json requirements.json README.md docs/adr/0016-x.md scripts/host-adapters.py` → OK); no new test directory — each change extends the suite that already owns the file, so `ci-wiring-check.py` needs no new step; case U runs on a **full-tree** scratch copy (`cp -R` of the checkout minus `.git`, links preserved — the shape the spikes used), not on the `SOURCES`-only `scratch_tree`, because the new invariants resolve links into `skills/`, `scripts/` and `hooks/`. ### Acceptance criteria 1. AC1 — `python3 scripts/host-adapters.py check` exits 0 on the real tree, and exits 1 naming `plugins/lifecycle` and the offending path when, in a full-tree scratch copy, (a) `plugins/lifecycle/skills/create-issue` is removed, (b) `plugins/lifecycle/skills/migrate-legacy` is linked, (c) `plugins/lifecycle/skills/merge-pr` points at `../../../skills/create-issue`, (d) a `plugins/lifecycle/.mcp.json` exists, (e) a linked skill's `SKILL.md` names `/samples/x` and `plugins/lifecycle/samples` does not exist — while a `/docs/x.md` pointer in the same file is not refused. 2. AC2 — `python3 scripts/host-adapters.py build` writes `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` and `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-{worker,merge}.md`; `check` exits 1 naming any of them after a hand edit, and 0 after `build` again (the same round trip cases B and C already prove for the rule copies). 3. AC3 — `python3 -c 'import json; json.load(open("hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json"))'` succeeds; the file carries the `Bash`, `SessionStart` and `Stop` blocks of `hooks/claude-hooks.json` byte-for-byte and no block whose `matcher` is `Read`. 4. AC4 — `scripts/preflight.sh --json` on a PATH without `dotnet` reports the `dotnet SDK >= 8` check with `"requiredBy": ["migrate-legacy"]`, the text output prints `[hard-required by: migrate-legacy]` on that line, and the exit status stays 1. 5. AC5 — `tests/skills/test.sh` passes: both new `token` values are found in `migrate-legacy`'s `compatibility`. 6. AC6 — `python3 tests/adr/check-adrs.py` exits 0 with ADR 0016 present and indexed; `tests/host-adapters/test.sh` cases K, L and R pass with the new manifest and the new README line. 7. AC7 — (manual, recorded in the PR description) after `claude plugin marketplace add ` and `claude plugin install ai-lifecycle-kit@ai-migration-kit-marketplace`, `claude plugin details ai-lifecycle-kit@ai-migration-kit-marketplace` lists exactly 12 components — the ten lifecycle skills plus `auto-dev-worker` and `auto-dev-merge` — hooks `PreToolUse` · `SessionStart` · `Stop`, and `MCP servers (0)`; the installed cache contains no symlink and no `migrate-legacy`. The spikes proved the local-path install only; the GitHub-URL install is re-checked after the release lands. ### Testing decisions **Seams under test:** `scripts/host-adapters.py check`'s exit code + `REFUSE:` lines on a scratch copy of the tree, and `build`'s written files; `scripts/preflight.sh --json`'s JSON and text output on a reduced PATH; `tests/adr/check-adrs.py`'s exit code. **Prior art:** `tests/host-adapters/test.sh` cases B/C (edit a derived file → refused → `build` restores), J, K, L, R and T already assert REFUSE lines over a scratch tree and read the marketplace by index; `tests/preflight/test.sh` case 4 already reduces PATH against the real `requirements.json` and greps `"status": "missing"`. **A good test here:** break one link in a scratch copy and assert `check` names that path — never assert on how `invariants()` builds its set (see `skills/_shared/test-seams.md`). ### Out of scope - The Codex marketplace (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`), the Copilot / Gemini / pi manifests and the rule-file hosts — they keep shipping the full kit; a lifecycle variant per host is a follow-up once the Claude Code plugin is proven with consumers. - Filtering the routing table `hooks/routing-context.sh` injects to the installed plugin's skills. - A Windows-safe copy-by-`build` variant of `plugins/lifecycle/` — the named upgrade path, filed when a Windows consumer asks. - Bundling AdrMcp in the lifecycle plugin — it would reintroduce `dnx`; the fallback the three skills already implement is the design. - Renaming `ai-migration-kit`, or splitting its version, its CHANGELOG or its release-please package (ADR 3). - Moving any file under `skills/`, `commands/`, `hooks/` or `scripts/`.
## 🛠️ Implementation plan > **For agentic workers:** execute this plan task-by-task with `implement-issue` (subagent-per-task for broad plans, inline for small ones). Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. **Goal:** a second plugin, `ai-lifecycle-kit`, served from `plugins/lifecycle/` as a manifest plus symlinks into the one tree, kept complete by `host-adapters.py check`, with preflight and the docs saying which skill owns the .NET prerequisites. **Architecture:** no file moves; `plugins/lifecycle/` holds a hand-written manifest, per-skill and per-directory symlinks, two derived command copies, and no `.mcp.json`; `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` is derived too — all three written by `host-adapters.py build`; the invariants that keep the tree complete live where the other manifest invariants live (`invariants()`); every test extends the suite that owns the file it touches. **Tech stack:** JSON manifests, git symlinks (mode `120000`, relative targets), bash (macOS 3.2-parseable), python3 (`host-adapters.py`, `check-adrs.py`), the kit's golden-test preamble `tests/_lib.sh`. **Seams under test:** `scripts/host-adapters.py check`'s exit code + `REFUSE:` lines on a full-tree scratch copy, and `build`'s written files; `scripts/preflight.sh --json`'s JSON and text output on a reduced PATH; `tests/adr/check-adrs.py`'s exit code. **Global Constraints:** - No file under `skills/`, `commands/`, `hooks/` or `scripts/` moves or is renamed (ADR 12: a skill name is an identifier six times over). - One version: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` are bumped by release-please only; `marketplace.json` carries no version (ADR 3, #556). - `requirements.json` is the single source of truth for prerequisites — never a hard-coded list; a `requiredBy` entry must carry a `token` found in that skill's `compatibility` (`tests/skills/check-frontmatter.py`). - Derived files (`gemini-extension.json`, `commands/*.toml`, the rule copies, and now `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` + `plugins/lifecycle/commands/*.md`) are written by `python3 scripts/host-adapters.py build`, never edited. - Every suite parses under macOS bash 3.2 (`./scripts/parse-sweep.sh`); every suite sources `tests/_lib.sh`; no new `tests//` directory, so `scripts/ci-wiring-check.py` is unchanged. - `hooks/hooks.json` must never exist (Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI auto-load that path — case I); `plugins/lifecycle/.mcp.json` must never exist (the lifecycle plugin launches no server). - Symlink targets are relative, never absolute; created with `ln -s`, committed as mode `120000`. - Commit identity: the profile's *Commit identity* section; commits through `guarded-commit.sh`. - Per-task test command: the suite named in the task; before ready: `./scripts/run-all-tests.sh`. - PR title: `feat(plugin): ship a lifecycle-only plugin beside the full kit (#)`. ### Task 1: `plugins/lifecycle/` — the manifest, the links, the derived files, and the invariants that keep it complete **Files:** create `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugins/lifecycle/skills/*` (11 symlinks), `plugins/lifecycle/hooks`, `plugins/lifecycle/scripts`, `plugins/lifecycle/decisions`, `plugins/lifecycle/templates`, `plugins/lifecycle/AGENTS.md`, `plugins/lifecycle/requirements.json`, `plugins/lifecycle/CONTEXT.md` (symlinks), `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` and `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-worker.md`, `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-merge.md` (via `build`); modify `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `release-please-config.json`, `scripts/host-adapters.py:63-80` (`VERSIONED`), `scripts/host-adapters.py:152-176` (`generated()`), `scripts/host-adapters.py:177-234` (`invariants()`); test `tests/host-adapters/test.sh`. **Interfaces:** produces the plugin `ai-lifecycle-kit` at `plugins/lifecycle/` (manifest fields as in the Spec); in `scripts/host-adapters.py` the constants `LIFECYCLE`, `MIGRATION_SKILLS`, `MIGRATION_COMMANDS`, three new `generated()` entries (`hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` from `hooks/claude-hooks.json`; `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-worker.md` and `auto-dev-merge.md` from `commands/`), the new `VERSIONED` path, and the five `REFUSE:` messages spelled exactly as the Spec lists them; `SOURCES` in the test gains `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json`, and a new helper `full_tree ` (`cp -R` of the checkout minus `.git`, links preserved) serves cases U and V. - [ ] **Step 1:** Write the failing case **U** in `tests/host-adapters/test.sh` (seam: `host-adapters.py check`'s exit code + `REFUSE:` lines on a full-tree scratch copy) — five scratch edits, each asserting exit 1 and a `REFUSE:` line naming `plugins/lifecycle` and the path: (a) `plugins/lifecycle/skills/create-issue` removed, (b) `plugins/lifecycle/skills/migrate-legacy` linked, (c) `plugins/lifecycle/skills/merge-pr` re-pointed at `../../../skills/create-issue`, (d) an empty `plugins/lifecycle/.mcp.json` created, (e) `/samples/x` **and** `/docs/x.md` appended to a linked skill's `SKILL.md` — refused for `samples/x` only; plus case **V**: `hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` and `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-worker.md` edited by hand → exit 1 naming each and its source; `build` → exit 0 (mirror cases B and C). Add the two new files to `SOURCES`; add the `full_tree` helper. - [ ] **Step 2:** Run `./tests/host-adapters/test.sh` → FAIL (U: `check` finds no `plugins/lifecycle`; V: no generated entries). - [ ] **Step 3:** Create the tree: `mkdir -p plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin plugins/lifecycle/skills plugins/lifecycle/commands`; `ln -s ../../../skills/ plugins/lifecycle/skills/` for `_shared auto-dev create-issue debug-issue deliver-issue implement-issue merge-pr profile-repo review-sessions setup-repo triage-backlog`; `ln -s ../../ plugins/lifecycle/` for `hooks scripts decisions templates AGENTS.md requirements.json CONTEXT.md`; write `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` exactly as the Spec's JSON with the version read from `.release-please-manifest.json`. No `.mcp.json`; the commands come from `build` in Step 4. - [ ] **Step 4:** In `scripts/host-adapters.py`: add `plugins/lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to `VERSIONED`; add to `generated()` the three derived files (`hooks/lifecycle-hooks.json` = `claude-hooks.json` minus the `PreToolUse` entry whose `matcher` is `Read`, `json.dumps(indent=2) + "\n"`; `plugins/lifecycle/commands/auto-dev-worker.md` and `auto-dev-merge.md` = the bytes of `commands/`); add the constants and the five refusals from the Spec to `invariants()`. Run `python3 scripts/host-adapters.py build`. - [ ] **Step 5:** Add `{"name": "ai-lifecycle-kit", "source": "./plugins/lifecycle", "description": …}` as `plugins[1]` of `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`; add the manifest to `release-please-config.json`'s `extra-files`; add a one-line assertion to case T that `plugins[1]["name"] == "ai-lifecycle-kit"` and `plugins[1]["source"] == "./plugins/lifecycle"`. - [ ] **Step 6:** Re-run `./tests/host-adapters/test.sh` → PASS (A, K, L, T on the real tree; U and V on the scratch edits); run `./scripts/parse-sweep.sh` and `python3 scripts/ci-wiring-check.py` → PASS. - [ ] **Step 7:** Manual proof, recorded in the PR description (AC7): `claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD"`, `claude plugin install ai-lifecycle-kit@ai-migration-kit-marketplace`, `claude plugin details ai-lifecycle-kit@ai-migration-kit-marketplace` → 12 components (ten skills + `auto-dev-worker` + `auto-dev-merge`), `PreToolUse` · `SessionStart` · `Stop`, `MCP servers (0)`; `find ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-migration-kit-marketplace/ai-lifecycle-kit -type l | wc -l` → 0. *Context*: the two halves named in `plugin.json`'s description, the four costs from this issue's Problem, and the three spikes' table; *Considered Options*: the three approaches from the Brainstorm; *Decision Outcome* (one paragraph): `plugins/lifecycle/` = manifest + symlinks over the one tree, one version, kept complete by `host-adapters.py check`; title: Adopt the harness effective-limit contract and align copied capability schemas
body:
## Outcome

Adopt the harness-published effective-limit contract in the Context Console and align this repository's copied capability/policy schemas with the harness producer, so the facade can admit context-memory and provider-session values only after authenticating them against the trusted descriptor.

The harness pin matrix (`sts2-harness` `contracts/effective-limits-pins.json`) records this repository as a **pending** consumer. No issue tracked that obligation until now.

## Current state — verified drift (console `main` @ `10122f38efce`)

| Surface | Console advertises | Console copied digest | Harness producer digest |
|---|---|---|---|
| context-memory | `ascension.context-memory.capabilities.v1`, `effective_limits_advertised: false` | `capabilities.schema.json` `c5558578…` | `2b980bbd…` (`v3`) |
| provider-session | `ascension.provider-session.capabilities.v1`, `effective_limits_advertised: false` | `capabilities.schema.json` `74504053…` | `de1348ec…` (`v3`) |
| provider-session policy | — | `678ce517…` | `48d6dc1c…` |
| context-memory policy | not copied | — | `55c9bba8…` |

The copied `$id`s are `urn:ascension:context-memory:capabilities:v1` / `urn:ascension:provider-session:capabilities:v1`; the producer contract is `v3`. The facade (`crates/context-service/src/harness_facade.rs`, `memory.rs`, `provider_session.rs`) does not consume `ascension.harness.effective-limits.v1`.

## Required implementation

1. Copy the harness producer artifacts (context-memory policy + capabilities, provider-session policy + capabilities) into `contracts/`, pinned by digest, and record the producer revision in `contracts/…/README.md`.
2. Advertise the aligned capability schema and an `effective_limits` classification (or an equivalent closed field) for each surface, keeping capture default-off and private retention approval-gated.
3. Consume the `ascension.harness.effective-limits.v1` record: authenticate it against the validated trusted descriptor (never the record under test), then admit a value before presenting it. A field absent from the record is unavailable, never unlimited.
4. Fail closed with machine-readable reasons (`effective_limit_exceeded`, `disabled`, `field_not_advertised`, `descriptor_stale`, `descriptor_tampered`, `profile_mismatch`, `consumer_not_recorded`, `consumer_pin_not_adopted`).
5. Publish the consumer evidence: versioned conformance fixtures, a focused test that fails if authentication or admission is removed, and pin verification against the copied bytes.
6. Update the harness pin-matrix consumer entry (revision, artifact inventory incl. context-memory policy, surfaces, `adoption: aligned`, and a `harness_ci_pin`) in a linked harness PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Advertised capability schema and copied artifact digests match the harness producer revision, verified by a test.
- [ ] A transparency/tamper test shows a record that keeps the trusted label but changes any limit, class, ceiling, `owner`, or `enabled` fails closed.
- [ ] A value above the executable ceiling is never presented as supported; unavailable reasons are machine-readable.
- [ ] Consumer evidence is recorded as synthetic/fixture-level only; real-owner/native/provider claims remain `unverified`.
- [ ] The harness pin matrix lists this consumer as aligned on the tested revision.

## Compatibility and decisions required

This changes a **public capability schema version** (`v1` → the harness `v3` contract) and the copied contract pins, which are root-owned. Before implementation, record the owner/consumer decision and compatibility classification, and coordinate the Studio consumer (also recorded `pending`) so both move together. This issue specifies requirements; it does not authorize deployment, provider/game calls, or private retention.

## Dependencies

- `sts2-harness#95` (producer contract; harness side merged in #165).
- Related: this issue's parent facade work (`#18`), the harness context-owner binding (`sts2-harness#100`, dispatch binding merged), and `ascension-workflow-studio`'s consumer entry.

title: Epic: resource metadata on the wire, the 1.0.0 label schema
body:
Tracking issue for the 1.0.0 label schema. The design is `docs/design/metadata-on-the-wire.html` on branch `docs/metadata-design-decisions` (PR #196); its four open questions were resolved on 2026-09-14 and are recorded in its §11. The OpenSpec change is `metadata-on-the-wire`; each sub-issue below is one task group of it.

## Why

OpenNMS resource metadata does not fit on Prometheus data series. The attribute key space is unbounded, so one label name per string attribute grows the backend's label-name index without limit (#112). And a label set is a series identity, so a mutable attribute on the data series forks history the moment a network operator sets or improves an interface description, an action nothing suggests could affect monitoring. `labels.attr-mode` with an allowlist addresses the first problem and not the second.

## Goals and constraints

- **Data series identity depends on nothing an operator edits.** `ifAlias` and `ifDescr` leave the data series on principle, not pending a churn number. `if_name` is the only interface label that stays.
- **Every attribute reaches Prometheus under a fixed set of label names**, as rows: `onms_resource_attr{resourceId, key, value} 1` and `onms_resource_category{resourceId, category} 1`, bounded by a per-resource budget of 16 with the remainder counted.
- **A fresh install has a usable join surface**: `onms_resource_info{resourceId, …} 1` from `metadata.info-columns = column=key, …`, default `if_alias=ifAlias, if_descr=ifDescr, resource_name=name`. Numerics are gauges (`onms_resource_ifspeed`), never label values.
- **OpenNMS graph placeholders resolve from rows**, so nothing needs curating for correctness: `findMetrics` enriches its results with one batched `onms_resource_attr` query per call, no plugin-side cache.
- **No database, no recording rules, no rule evaluator** on the critical path. Native PromQL uses one `group_left` join.
- **Greenfield.** No compatibility with the v0.x schema, no dual emission, no read-path support for the old prefixes. `labels.attr-mode`, `labels.attr-include`, `labels.categories-mode`, the `onms_attr_*`, `onms_extattr_*`, `onms_cat_*`, `categories`, `if_descr`, `if_speed` and `_idx*` labels are removed.

## What the plugin emits

```
# data series: what is needed to read them, plus the stable promoted set
ifHCInOctets{resourceId="snmp/1/if1", mtype="counter", node_label="core-sw-1", if_name="Et1"}

# rows: every attribute, three label names forever
onms_resource_attr{resourceId="snmp/1/if1", key="ifAlias", value="uplink"} 1
onms_resource_attr{resourceId="snmp/1/if1", key="ifDescr", value="Ethernet1"} 1
onms_resource_category{resourceId="node/1", category="Production"} 1

# columns: the configured subset
onms_resource_info{resourceId="snmp/1/if1", if_alias="uplink", if_descr="Ethernet1"} 1

# numerics
onms_resource_ifspeed{resourceId="snmp/1/if1"} 1000000000
```

Metadata series are emitted on first sight, on change, and otherwise every `metadata.cadence` (default 15 minutes), in their own batches through the existing write pipeline.

## Decisions already made

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| ifAlias placement | Principle: never on a data series, whatever the churn rate. Same for ifDescr (it embeds the description on Nokia SR OS and some Huawei releases, and follows renames on RouterOS and Linux). |
| Default columns and budget | `if_alias=ifAlias, if_descr=ifDescr, resource_name=name`; budget 16. Sub-resource names under collector-specific keys (`hrStorageDescr`, `dskPath`, `datname`) are one config entry away; a "first key that looks like a name" rule was rejected. |
| Read-path caching | None. One batched query per `findMetrics` call; OpenNMS already caches in front of `findMetrics`, and a plugin cache would serve a stale alias after exactly the operator action this design protects against. |
| `@` modifier | Available on Prometheus ≥ 2.33, Mimir, VictoriaMetrics ≥ 1.72.0, Cortex ≥ 1.18 (or `-querier.at-modifier-enabled` on 1.8 to 1.17). Only the historical-correctness idiom uses it. |

## Cutover, not migration

Series written before 1.0.0 keep their old identity for the retention window and are not joined to the new ones. Dashboards that filtered on a removed label move to the `group_left` idiom. OpenNMS graph rendering is unaffected across the boundary, because the read path resolves resources by `__name__` and `resourceId`, which stay. Stated once, in the release note.

## Out of scope

- `labels.profile=legacy` (compatibility with the other plugin's wire schema) is a separate decision and is not settled here.
- Changes to the write pipeline (shards, tiers, flusher). Metadata samples ride it unchanged.

## Deliveries, in order

Sub-issues are linked below. Each follows the repo workflow: `/opsx:apply` on the `metadata-on-the-wire` change for its task group, `/code-review medium`, a PR that closes the sub-issue, merge on green, tick here.

- [ ] #190 D1: rows, registry and emitter
- [ ] #191 D2: columns and the speed gauge
- [ ] #192 D3: read-path enrichment from rows
- [ ] #193 D4: removal of the v0.x attribute mechanisms
- [ ] #194 D5: documentation and changelog
- [ ] #195 D6: end-to-end assertions and a Grafana example
- [ ] 1.0.0 release

title: The Account Center menu is processed twice per page render, so every entry's visibility check runs twice
body:
Every page in the Account Center processes `AccountCenterMenu` twice for one render:

- `get_active_section()` calls `AccountCenterMenu.process(request)` to resolve the section for the trail (`mvp/menus.py`, reached from `AccountPageMixin.get_breadcrumbs`).
- `<c-account.nav>` calls `{% process_menu "AccountCenterMenu" as account_menu %}` to draw the panel (`mvp/templates/cotton/account/nav.html`).

Processing a menu evaluates every entry's `check(request)`. The documented use for a check is deciding whether an entry applies to the person making the request, which is exactly the kind of question that reaches the database. Those queries are paid twice per page, and the duplication grows with the number of entries an app contributes rather than staying constant.

Nothing is wrong today: the menu is small and the checks in the test suite are pure functions. It is worth fixing before a project with a real permission check adopts the area, and the shape of the fix is to process once per request and share the result rather than to make each caller cheaper.

Found during the review of #342, recorded rather than fixed there: the fix changes how the view and the panel share state, which is more than that feature needed.

title: Publish the WAL replay permit gate ceiling and available-permit count
body:
## Summary

The per-silo WAL replay concurrency gate (`BPlusLeafGrain._replayConcurrencyGate`)
publishes how many permits have been **withheld** by memory backpressure, but
never publishes **how many there were to begin with**. That makes the withheld
count uninterpretable, and it is currently the single number blocking a
diagnosis of estate-wide leaf stranding.

Add two instruments:

1. `orleans.lattice.wal.replay.permit_ceiling` (gauge, `{permit}`) - the size the
   gate was sized to by `ResolveReplayConcurrencyGate`.
2. `orleans.lattice.wal.replay.permits_available` (gauge, `{permit}`) - the gate's
   current `CurrentCount`.

Both measure a **level**, not a distribution, so both zero-prime correctly. This
is deliberately not a histogram - see the shape/level rule below.

## Why this is blocking

From the run-16 scrape of the deployed container, aggregated over **all 64
shards** (denominator asserted):

```
orleans_lattice_wal_replay_permits_withheld{tenant="_platform_"}      1
..._permit_adaptations_total{outcome="withheld",trigger="occupancy"}  1
..._permit_adaptations_total{outcome="withheld",trigger="fault"}      0
..._permit_adaptations_total{outcome="restored"}                      0
```

One permit was withheld by memory-occupancy backpressure and never restored.
`restored` is zero-primed, so that zero is measured, not absent.

**One withheld out of 16 is noise. One withheld out of 2 is half the estate's
replay throughput.** Nothing in the container distinguishes these. The gate is
sized from `min(Environment.ProcessorCount, enforced container CPU grant)`
(#2816) and, per the comment at `BPlusLeafGrain.Activation.cs:1220-1221`, is
"sized once ... and is never re-created or topped up".

## The observability gap this sits inside

A permanently queued activation is **invisible in every existing series**.
Ordering in `BPlusLeafGrain.Activation.cs`:

| line | site |
|---|---|
| `:811` | `await gate.WaitAsync(cancellationToken)` |
| `:815` | on `OperationCanceledException` -> record permit wait, arm `canceled` |
| `:819` | on success -> record permit wait, arm `acquired` |
| `:1268` | `LeafActivationReplays.Add(...)` |

Both permit-wait recording sites and the replay-start counter are **downstream of
the wait**. An activation still queued therefore records neither its wait nor a
replay start. The source already names the symptom, at `:1225`:

> "...stop the silo activating leaves entirely, and the symptom is a silent wait
> on WaitAsync rather than an error."

Two consequences, both observed in run 16:

**The permit-wait mean is censored.** `repo-context-vector-index` reports a mean
queue wait of 574,077 ms over a `_count` of **29** - but that is the mean over
the 29 activations that eventually acquired. Anything still waiting is excluded
from numerator and denominator alike. The exported summary carries only `_sum`
and `_count`; `quantile=` appears **zero** times across all 18 series lines, so
there is no p99 or max to fall back on either.

**Two trees are entirely silent while stranding in every shard.** Aggregated over
all 64 shards:

| | `repo-context-content` | `repo-context-vector-metadata` | `repo-context-vector-index` | `repo-context-memory` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| durable WAL bytes | 3,090,785 | 9,814,220 | 37,923,264,125 | 1,337,423 |
| stranded | 1,216 | 640 | 2,093 | 0 |
| shards stranding | 64/64 | 64/64 | 57/64 | 0/64 |
| permit acquisitions | absent | absent | 29 | 64 |
| replay starts | absent | absent | 29 | 64 |
| distinct metric families | 27 | 27 | 84 | 102 |

`content` and `vector-metadata` hold durable WAL data, so "empty tree strands
spuriously" is refuted. They emit only the 27 metric families that do not require
a leaf activation, against 84 and 102 for trees that do activate. Together they
are **47% of estate stranding** (3,985 total) with **no leaf activation ever
recorded**.

Additionally, every one of the 18 permit-wait series carries
`outcome="acquired"`; there is **not a single `canceled` series**. Since `:815`
records that arm whenever it fires, its absence means no queued activation was
ever cancelled - the ones missing from the acquired count were, at scrape time,
**still queued**.

## Scope

- Publish both gauges from `ResolveReplayConcurrencyGate` / the gate holder.
- Zero-prime both. They measure a level, so a published zero is meaningful.
- **Do not** add a histogram or any distribution-shaped instrument here. Priming
  an instrument that measures a *shape* fabricates a sample and biases the
  distribution; priming one that measures a *level* does not. See the decision
  recorded on #3044.
- Docs row in `docs/lattice/metrics.md` and dashboard panel per the per-package
  fixtures - the enrolment gates pass regardless of whether those exist, so they
  must be added deliberately.
- Enrol both in `InstrumentPrimingEnrolment.tsv` as `primed`.
- Run the repository-wide metric gates **individually**; OR-ing them into one
  filter crashes the vstest host and misattributes the failure.

## Out of scope

- Partitioning or resizing the gate. That is #3043 and is a behaviour change;
  this issue is observability only and must not alter admission.
- The stranding cause itself. This issue makes the leading hypothesis testable;
  it does not adjudicate it.
- `repo-context-structural`'s 36 stranded events across 36 shards, on a 49 ms
  mean with a full 64/64 permit acquisition. It got its permits, so its stranding
  has a separate cause. Parked deliberately, not folded in.

## Acceptance

- Both gauges present in a container scrape, with a non-zero ceiling.
- `withheld` becomes interpretable: ceiling minus withheld minus available
  reconciles against the number of in-flight replays.
- No change to admission behaviour; the gate's sizing logic is untouched.

title: Move session logic into a framework-free native core, then expose it to plain iOS and Android apps
body:
Cordierite's daemon, CLI and MCP server are already framework-agnostic: the app talks plain JSON over a pinned `wss://` socket ([`docs/PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/callstackincubator/cordierite/blob/main/docs/PROTOCOL.md)), and `packages/cordierite/src/__tests__/e2e/app-client.ts` drives a full session from Node without touching anything React Native. The only thing tying Cordierite to React Native is *where the app-side logic lives*: about half of it is already RN-free Swift/Kotlin, the other half is TypeScript in `@cordierite/react-native`.

This issue proposes finishing that split — move the remaining session logic into native, reduce the RN package to a thin bridge — and then expose the native core directly to plain iOS and Android apps.

## Where things stand today

**Already RN-free (native):**

- `ios/CordieriteConnectionManager.swift` imports only Foundation, Security and CryptoKit; `android/.../CordieriteConnectionManager.kt` imports only Android + OkHttp. Between them: TLS, SPKI pinning, trust-mode resolution from the Info.plist / manifest keys, the private-LAN check, keepalive, building `session_claim` / `session_resume` (including the `device_*` fields), parsing `session_ack`, and the process-memory resume lease store.
- RN coupling is confined to four thin files: `CordieriteTurboBridge.swift` + `RCTNativeCordierite.mm` on iOS, `NativeCordieriteModule.kt` + `CordieritePackage.kt` on Android (~500 lines total).

**Still in TypeScript (`packages/react-native/src`):**

| Concern | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session lifecycle | `client/index.ts`, `client/backoff.ts`, `client/terminal-close.ts`, `client/resume-lease.ts` | full-jitter reconnect, grace timer, foreground/background, restore-from-lease on startup, terminal-close classification |
| Tool registry | `client/registry.ts` | snapshot on every claim/resume, deltas on register/unregister |
| Tool invocation | `client/tool-invocation.ts` | per-tool timeout, `tool_cancel` → abort, progress, the seven `tool_error` types |
| Bootstrap | `bootstrap.ts`, `deep-link-core.ts`, `deep-link-install.ts` | URL parse, binary payload decode (`@cordierite/shared`), expiry + private-IP check, "a delivered link outranks a held session" |
| Schemas | `schema.ts` (~590 lines) | Standard Schema / Zod → JSON Schema, input/output validation — inherently JS |

## Proposal

### Phase 1 — extract a core target (mechanical, no behaviour change)

- iOS: move `CordieriteConnectionManager.swift` + `CordieriteProcessResumeLeaseStore.swift` into a `CordieriteCore` target with a SwiftPM manifest and its own podspec. `Cordierite.podspec` depends on it and keeps only the bridge files.
- Android: move `src/debug/java` (minus the RN module/package classes) into a separate `cordierite-core` Gradle module with no `react-android` dependency. The RN module depends on it.
- Keep `CordieriteNativeMarker` (and its consumer keep rule) in core, and add an iOS equivalent, so `cordierite doctor` has an anchor that does not depend on the RN class name `RCTNativeCordierite` (`packages/cordierite/src/artifact-inspect.ts`).
- Existing Swift/Kotlin tests move with the code; the RN package's test suite is the regression check.

### Phase 2 — move session logic into core

Port the TypeScript concerns above into `CordieriteCore` (Swift) and `cordierite-core` (Kotlin). The TurboModule surface shrinks to roughly:

```ts
registerTool(descriptor: ToolDescriptorJson): void;   // name, description, input/output JSON Schema, annotations, timeout_ms
unregisterTool(name: string): void;
handleUrl(url: string): boolean;                       // bootstrap deep link
postEvent(name: string, payloadJson: string): void;
respondToToolCall(id: string, resultJson: string | null, errorJson: string | null): void;
onToolCall: EventEmitter<{ id, name, argsJson }>;      // native → JS: run the handler
onToolCancel: EventEmitter<{ id }>;                    // native → JS: abort the handler's signal
onStateChange / onError                                // as today
```

JS keeps what is genuinely JS: `useCordieriteTool`, Standard Schema → JSON Schema export, validating handler input/output against the registered schema, and the Metro strip helper. Timeouts, cancellation, progress, reconnect, lease restore and registry snapshots all become native and identical across RN and native consumers.

Parity is the risk here. The unit tests in `packages/react-native/src/__tests__` (`client.test.ts`, `tool-invocation.test.ts`, `backoff.test.ts`, `bootstrap.test.ts`, `deep-link-bootstrap.test.ts`) are the spec to port. The SPKI pin tests already share one hardcoded vector across TS, Swift and Kotlin; extend that into a shared fixtures directory (bootstrap payloads, frame shapes, close-code handling) that all three test suites read.

### Phase 3 — native entry points and packaging

Public API sketch. iOS:

```swift
import Cordierite

@main struct MyApp: App {
  init() {
    Cordierite.shared.register(
      name: "seed_cart",
      description: "Fill the cart with test items.",
      inputSchema: ["type": "object", "properties": ["items": ["type": "number"]], "required": ["items"]]
    ) { args in
      ["added": args["items"] ?? 0]
    }
  }

  var body: some Scene {
    WindowGroup {
      ContentView().onOpenURL { Cordierite.shared.handle($0) }
    }
  }
}
```

The app declares its URL scheme in `CFBundleURLTypes` (most apps already do) and, for hardened builds, the existing `CordieriteTrust` / `CordieriteCliPins` / `CordieriteAllowPrivateLanOnly` keys — same keys core reads today. Lease restore on launch happens on first access to `Cordierite.shared`; foreground/background observation moves into core via `UIApplication` notifications.

Android:

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
dependencies { debugImplementation("com.callstackincubator.cordierite:core:<version>") }
android { defaultConfig { manifestPlaceholders["cordieriteScheme"] = "myapp" } }
```

```kotlin
class App : Application() {
  override fun onCreate() {
    super.onCreate()
    Cordierite.register(
      name = "seed_cart",
      description = "Fill the cart with test items.",
      inputSchema = JSONObject("""{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"number"}},"required":["items"]}"""),
    ) { args -> JSONObject().put("added", args.optInt("items")) }
  }
}
```

The library manifest ships a no-UI trampoline activity with an `<intent-filter>` on `${cordieriteScheme}`, so the app never forwards `onNewIntent`. The existing manifest `<meta-data>` trust keys stay as they are.

Also in this phase:

- Publish `CordieriteCore` via SwiftPM tag + CocoaPods, and `cordierite-core` to Maven Central; the RN package pins exact versions.
- `cordierite doctor`: detect the core marker on both platforms.
- `cordierite init` / scheme discovery: optionally read `CFBundleURLTypes` from an Xcode project's Info.plist and the `cordieriteScheme` placeholder or intent filter from a Gradle project, alongside today's `app.json` step. `--scheme`, `CORDIERITE_SCHEME` and `.cordierite/config.json` already work for native apps with no changes.
- Native playground apps (SwiftUI + Compose) next to the Expo one; docs for both platforms.

## Open questions

1. **Schema DX on native.** v1 accepts raw JSON Schema (dictionary / `JSONObject`); no input validation on the app side (the daemon does none either). A Swift macro / Kotlin annotation processor deriving schemas from `Codable` / `kotlinx.serialization` types is a plausible follow-up but not needed to ship.
2. **Compile-out story for native apps.** `debugImplementation` covers Android. SwiftPM cannot restrict a dependency per configuration the way CocoaPods `:configurations` does; document a `#if DEBUG` wrapper or a separate app target, and rely on `cordierite doctor --assert-absent` as the gate ([`docs/BUILD-VARIANTS.md`](https://github.com/callstackincubator/cordierite/blob/main/docs/BUILD-VARIANTS.md)).
3. **Handler threading.** Native handlers: main actor / main thread by default with an async variant, or always background? RN handlers run on the JS thread, which sidesteps the question today.
4. **Do phases 1–2 ship as a breaking `@cordierite/react-native` release?** The public JS API (`useCordieriteTool`, `registerTool`, `postEvent`, listeners) can stay identical; only the TurboModule spec changes, which is internal.

## Out of scope

- Flutter / KMP / other frameworks — they can consume the same core targets later.
- Changing the wire protocol or the daemon. Nothing here touches `packages/cordierite`.

title: Connector: Microsoft Teams channel messages
body:
**Source:** Microsoft Teams channel messages, through Microsoft Graph.

Teams is where many site questions get asked now, including the ones that turn into claims. This one needs more care than the others (admin-consented permissions, change notifications), so it is marked **help wanted** rather than good first issue.

## What it should do
- Delegated Graph permission `ChannelMessage.Read.All` (requires tenant admin consent), plus `offline_access`. Nothing that can write.
- The connection names the team and channel(s) to watch.
- Poll channel messages and replies with delta paging; emit a signal per message that mentions the connected user or matches the existing notice/RFI/change-order cues.
- Optional second step: Graph change notifications for channel messages, following how the Outlook connector handles subscriptions and `clientState`.
- `external_id` from the message id.

## Reference
The Outlook connector in `backend/osprey/connectors/` already does Graph OAuth, delta queries, subscriptions and renewal; much of it carries over. Test with a Microsoft 365 developer tenant, never a production one.

## How to build it
- Start from the template: [`connectors-sdk/`](https://github.com/ibuilder/osprey/tree/main/connectors-sdk) (Quick start, then *The interface*).
- Ship it as a plugin registered on the `osprey.connectors` entry point. **No edits to Osprey core.**

body:
**Use case**

A minimal table — one non-sortable, non-filterable, non-groupable column (a search-results list, name + thumbnail only) — where the Columns/Sort/Filter buttons have nothing to act on, and the toolbar's own "Search…" box duplicates a real search input already elsewhere on the page (confusingly, right above it in our case).

**Current workaround**

```css
.my-page .dt-toolbar { display: none; }
```

title: Connector: Smartsheet (read-only, due rows)

title: Feature request: public API to focus/scroll to a specific row from outside the table
body:
**Use case**

A page where the table isn't the only navigation surface — ours opens a side panel/lightbox for the clicked row, and that panel/lightbox has its own prev/next/random controls that can change "the current game" without any click on the table itself. We want the table's own roving-tabindex "current row" (and viewport scroll) to follow along, so:
- the highlighted/focused row always matches whatever's open elsewhere on the page,
- and if the user then Tabs into the table or uses the keyboard, they land where they'd expect.

**Current workaround**

Since there's no public API for this, we're reaching into the rendered DOM directly:

```js
const row = container.querySelector(`tr.dt-tr[data-row-key="${id}"]`);
row?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
row?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' });
```

This works today because the row component listens for any real `focus` event (not just ones from its own keyboard handlers), so calling `.focus()` correctly updates the internal roving-tabindex state. But it depends on `dt-tr`, an internal class name not documented anywhere as part of the public API — a future refactor could rename it with no type error to catch the breakage on our end.

**Request**

Some supported way to set/read "the current row" from outside the table, e.g. mirroring `TableState.selection`'s shape:

```ts
table.focus.current: Accessor<TRow | null>
table.focus.set(rowIdOrRow): void
```

or, if a full reactive API is more than you want to commit to, at least documenting `data-row-key` + a stable class name as the supported way to do this via `.focus()`, so consumers aren't relying on an implementation detail.

(Tangential, not asking you to solve it here: the current DOM approach also only works for a row on the currently visible page — a row elsewhere would need `table.pagination.setPage(...)` first, and there's no public way to compute which page a given row id is on either.)

Happy to open a PR if a shape like this sounds right.

title: Connector: Primavera P6 schedule export (.xer)
body:
**Source:** Oracle Primavera P6 schedule exports (`.xer`). No API, no credentials: the file itself is the source.

Schedules are where a slipping critical activity first shows up, long before anyone emails about it. P6's XER export is tab-delimited text: `%T` starts a table, `%F` names its fields, `%R` rows follow.

- Accept an XER file through the forward/file-drop path (`POST /connections/{id}/forward`), the way the Argus connector accepts CSV exports.

  - not complete, with a finish date in the next 14 days or already past;
  - negative total float (it is driving a delay).
- Title from the activity code and name; `due_at` from the early/late finish; body notes float and status.
- Re-sending the same export must create nothing new: build `external_id` from the project and activity ids.

The Argus connector, `backend/osprey/connectors/argus/__init__.py`, is the closest existing example: an export with no API, parsed leniently, deduplicated on re-send.

title: VersionControl: control worktree garbage, including Rust build output
body:
## Summary

A machine-wide sweep on 2026-09-14 found worktree garbage in five repositories, in four distinct shapes. `GitWorktrees.md` already says "a merged worktree that outlives its merge" is a red flag, and it ties removal to "the session that merges the pull request". That single hook did not fire in any of the five cases. The skill needs an audit that runs independently of the merge session, a rule for repository moves, a rule against temporary locations, and a rule for build output. Rust build output is the expensive case.

## What the sweep found

| Shape                                   | Evidence                                                                                                                                                     | Age when found          |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| Merged worktree outlives its merge      | Two submodules of one superproject each kept `.worktrees/<branch>` after the matching merge requests merged on 2026-08-19.                                     | 26 days                 |
| Merged or closed, and the repo moved    | A repo moved one directory level. Two `.git/worktrees/*/gitdir` pointers and both `.worktrees/*/.git` files still named the old path. `git status` inside the checkouts failed with `fatal: not a git repository: (null)`. The merge requests had merged on 2026-07-31 and closed on 2026-08-01. | 44 to 45 days           |
| Unpushed work only in worktrees         | Three worktrees, each with one commit from 2026-09-07 that exists on no remote and has no pull request. The primary checkout sat on a fourth work branch.     | 7 days                  |
| Worktree in a temporary directory       | One live worktree registered at `/private/tmp/claude-501/<session>/scratchpad/<name>`. The branch has an open merge request. A temp sweep would leave a dangling registration. | live                    |

The two jj colocated repositories on the same machine had only their default workspaces. jj was clean.

## Gaps in the current skill

1. **No audit outside the merge session.** Cleanup lives in `GitWorktrees.md` under "Cleanup" and is owed by the session that merges. A merge through the web UI, a closed pull request, or a session that ends early leaves nothing to catch the leftover later. Four of the five cases above are exactly this.
2. **No rule for repository moves.** `git worktree repair` relinks both directions after a move. The skill does not mention it. An agent that meets a `prunable` entry today has two wrong options: prune metadata for a checkout that still exists, or leave it.
3. **Directory selection permits a temp path.** "Directory selection" lists `.worktrees/`, a documented location, or ask. It does not forbid `$TMPDIR`, the harness scratchpad, or any path outside the repository. The scratchpad case above shows that agents do pick it.
4. **No end-of-session inventory of unpushed work.** The skill assumes every worktree ends "merged or abandoned". The three unpushed commits were neither. Nothing asks the agent to push, open a pull request, or hand the decision to the user before the session ends.
5. **Build output multiplies with worktrees.** "Create and prepare" tells the agent to run `cargo build` in every new worktree. Cargo writes to `<checkout>/target` by default, so every worktree carries its own full build. The "Supersession check" then asks the agent to "review every untracked file, including ignored files", which is not a meaningful instruction for a build directory.

Measured Rust `target/` sizes on the same machine (`du -sk`, 2026-09-14):

| Project                       | `target/` size |
| ----------------------------- | -------------- |
| Tauri desktop app             | 4.8 GB         |
| forge-cli                     | 1.9 GB         |
| Rust mail connector           | 1.4 GB         |

None of the five repositories in the sweep is a Rust project, so the multiplication is a projection, not an observation. Under the assumption that a worktree build is as large as the primary build, three worktrees of forge-cli add about 5.7 GB (3 × 1.9 GB) of disposable output that `git worktree list` never shows.

## Proposed changes

- **Add an audit step** to `GitWorktrees.md` and to `Jujutsu.md`, to run at the start of any VersionControl task and at the end of every session that created a worktree:

    ```sh
    git worktree list --porcelain
    git worktree prune -n
    jj workspace list          # colocated repos only
    ```

    For each non-primary entry: name the branch, its upstream, and the pull request state from the platform (not from ancestry, per the existing squash-merge note). Classify as live, merged, closed, or unpushed. Remove merged and closed after the existing supersession check. Report unpushed to the user with push, open a pull request, or drop as the choices.

- **Add a repository-move rule.** When `git worktree prune -n` lists an entry whose checkout directory still exists, run `git worktree repair <path>` first, then classify. Prune only entries whose directory is gone. Reference: [git-worktree][GITWT].

- **Forbid temporary locations.** Add to "Directory selection": never place a worktree under `$TMPDIR`, the harness scratchpad, or any path outside the repository's ignored worktree root. Add "a worktree in a temporary directory" to "Red flags".

- **Handle build output.** In "Create and prepare", set a shared target directory before the first Rust build in a worktree, so all worktrees of one repository reuse one build cache:

    ```sh
    export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)/../target"
    ```

    Verified on git 2.55.0: from a worktree this resolves to `<primary checkout>/target`. In a submodule the common dir sits under the superproject's `.git/modules/`, so name the submodule's primary checkout explicitly there. Cargo serializes builds on the shared directory with its own lock, so parallel worktree builds wait for each other. Where that is unacceptable, keep per-worktree output and run `cargo clean` before `git worktree remove`. Reference: [CARGO_TARGET_DIR][CARGOENV], [build.target-dir][CARGOCFG]. In "Supersession check", classify `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `dist/`, and `build/` as disposable build output that needs no per-file review.

## Acceptance

- A repository with a merged worktree and no merge session in progress: the audit step lists it and removes it.
- A repository moved one directory level: the audit step repairs the links and `git status` works in the checkout again.
- A worktree under `$TMPDIR`: the audit step reports it as a red flag.
- A Rust repository with two worktrees: `du -s` shows one `target/` directory, not three.

[GITWT]: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree "git-worktree documentation"
[CARGOENV]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html "Cargo environment variables"
[CARGOCFG]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildtarget-dir "Cargo configuration: build.target-dir"
